harbor.practice: Harbor's small guardrail classifier is a 2-layer MLP over sentence embeddings; its training loss is CrossEntropyLoss on raw logits.
harbor.failure: Applying softmax before a loss that expects logits.

harbor.practice: Harbor's reranker fine-tune uses AdamW, 5% warm-up, cosine decay and gradient accumulation to reach an effective batch of 64 on a single GPU.
harbor.failure: Changing the batch size without retuning the learning rate, then blaming the data when training becomes unstable.

harbor.practice: A Harbor training run produced NaN at step 3,100. The cause was one 40,000-token corrupted document; length filtering plus gradient clipping fixed it, not a lower learning rate alone.
harbor.failure: Using clipping to hide a data or loss bug: it treats the symptom, not the cause.

harbor.practice: Harbor's general embedding model placed "PTO" far from "annual leave". A domain-tuned embedding (13.5) fixed the internal acronyms that a general model had never seen.
harbor.failure: Using an LLM's internal hidden states as search embeddings without evaluating them; general hidden vectors are not automatically good retrieval vectors.

harbor.practice: Harbor's document pipeline still uses a CNN-based layout detector to find tables in scanned PDFs before any transformer sees the text.
harbor.failure: Assuming an LSTM (or any model) remembers arbitrarily long inputs reliably.

harbor.practice: Every Harbor training script first overfits 8 examples to near-zero loss, then saves and reloads a checkpoint and compares predictions, before the real run starts.
harbor.failure: Saving a checkpoint and never reloading it: a file that cannot be restored is not a checkpoint.
